newsitem.title: BELGIUM: European Union ministers threaten fur import ban.
newsitem.headline: European Union ministers threaten fur import ban.

text.p: European Union environment ministers threatened on Monday to impose an EU import ban on fur from animals caught in leg-hold traps unless negotiators from Canada, the United States and Russia accept tighter humane trapping standards, a British official told reporters.

The official said ministers, in a closed-door meeting, said an existing draft agreement on trapping standards was "completely unacceptable" and said they had asked the European Commission to prepare a ban to start as soon as possible.

Negotiators from the four sides have been in talks for months over improved trapping standards in an effort to avert a fur import ban already agreed by the EU, preventing the ban coming into force while negotiations continued.
The talks aim to lay down standards for traps which kill or catch 18 species of wild animals including muskrats, beavers, sable, lynx and wolves.

Canada and Russia had accepted the draft deal on trapping standards but the United States thought even that went too far. EU rejection of the compromise means that all three will have to return to talks to avoid being hit by the threatened ban.

Another EU diplomat had earlier told reporters the draft four-way deal "appeared unacceptable to a number of countries", citing Britain, Germany, the Netherlands, Italy and Austria as among the most critical.

Those countries alone carry sufficient voting weight to block the draft agreement as negotiated by the Commission, which now faces pressure to draw up plans for a ban, a process which would take at least three months.

National and international animal welfare groups had already damned the draft standards as a "cynical political solution" to U.S. threats of World Trade Organisation retaliation if the EU ban went ahead.
Demonstrators dressed as bloodstained furry creatures greeted environment ministers as they arrived for their scheduled meeting on Monday.
